title: Figure 13: Orbital inclination vs. lateral range, orbits required to land in CA or FL
description: Chart titled "Time (orbits) Required to Land in California or Florida; Orbital Altitude is 200 nautical miles," plotting orbital inclination (degrees, 0-100) against spacecraft lateral range (nautical miles, 0-5000). Curves are labeled 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 14 orbits, with shaded bands for "Apollo" (red), "Nominal Lifting Body" (green) and "Model 176 Operating Envelope" (blue), plus "Minimum lateral Range For Once A Day Landing" and "Maximum Waiting Time" labels. Caption: "Figure 13. Sufficient Cross Range (L/D) Means There is No Waiting to Return."
